compliance.regulatoryHistory: In May 2023, Chinese state security authorities raided Capvision offices as part of a broader crackdown on consulting firms. Capvision subsequently completed a government-supervised rectification process and implemented comprehensive compliance reforms. Separately, the firm has faced scrutiny from Western regulators regarding cross-border information flows.

overview:
Capvision is one of the largest expert networks headquartered in Asia and the largest expert network based in China, where it is domestically known as Kaisheng Rongying (凯盛融英). Founded in 2006 by former Bain & Company consultants and Morgan Stanley investment bankers, the firm has built deep expertise in connecting global institutional clients with industry professionals across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond. Capvision partners with over 2,000 clients including institutional investors, consulting firms, and Fortune 500 companies, and facilitated approximately 150,000 consulting calls annually as of 2021–2022.

The company offers a broad suite of primary research services including expert consultations, surveys, corporate access events, customized research projects, and industry reports. With offices in Shanghai, New York, Munich, Hong Kong, Osaka, and Beijing, Capvision straddles both Asian and Western markets — a positioning that is both its key differentiator and, following the 2023 Chinese government crackdown on consulting firms, a source of ongoing regulatory complexity. The company raised $56.6M in total funding and filed for a Hong Kong IPO in 2022 targeting a $1.5–3 billion valuation, though those plans were effectively shelved after the 2023 state security investigation.

history.narrative: Capvision was founded in 2006 in Shanghai by Roger Xu and Kai Hong, both of whom came from backgrounds in management consulting and investment banking. The firm originally focused on sourcing expert advisors within China for global institutional clients, and gradually expanded its network and geographic footprint. By the early 2020s Capvision had grown to 600+ employees and was positioning for a Hong Kong IPO. However, the company's trajectory was significantly disrupted in 2023 when Chinese state security authorities raided its offices as part of a broader crackdown on consulting and due diligence firms operating in China.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Consultations
servicesDetailed.description: One-on-one or group consultations connecting clients with industry professionals who have direct operational experience in specific sectors, companies, or markets. Capvision offers optional live language translation, making it particularly effective for cross-border research involving Asian markets. The firm facilitated approximately 150,000 consulting calls annually as of 2021–2022, with experts earning an average of $230 per hour.

servicesDetailed.name: Surveys
servicesDetailed.description: Quantitative and qualitative survey research leveraging Capvision's expert network to provide structured data on market conditions, competitive dynamics, and industry trends. Surveys can be paired with follow-up consultations for deeper investigation.

servicesDetailed.name: Industry Reports
servicesDetailed.description: Capvision produces and distributes industry-focused research reports drawing on its expert network and primary research capabilities, covering sectors across Asia and global markets.

servicesDetailed.name: Corporate Access / Events
servicesDetailed.description: Conferences, roundtables, and corporate access events that bring together industry experts, company management teams, and institutional investors. These events are particularly focused on Asian markets and cross-border investment themes.

servicesDetailed.name: Customized Research
servicesDetailed.description: Bespoke research projects combining expert consultations, surveys, and desk research into comprehensive deliverables tailored to specific client questions — often used for due diligence, market entry analysis, and competitive intelligence.

servicesDetailed.name: HR & Talent Services
servicesDetailed.description: Executive search and talent advisory services that leverage Capvision's expert network for recruitment and organizational consulting.

aiPlatform.narrative: Capvision's technology infrastructure centers on a proprietary CRM system that manages expert matching, client relationships, and project workflows. The platform integrates third-party tools including Confirmit, Qualtrics, and ZoomInfo for survey delivery, data enrichment, and expert sourcing. While Capvision markets AI-assisted matching and automated compliance checks, detailed public documentation of specific AI capabilities is limited compared to some Western competitors. The platform also includes a mobile knowledge app for on-demand expert content delivery.

complianceExtended.narrative: Capvision's compliance story is uniquely complex due to its position straddling Chinese and international regulatory environments. Following the May 2023 raid by Chinese state security authorities, the firm underwent a government-supervised rectification process and announced comprehensive compliance reforms. The company now operates under enhanced scrutiny in China while also maintaining compliance frameworks aligned with Western regulatory expectations around MNPI and expert vetting.
highlights: Dedicated compliance committee established in May 2023, chaired by CEO Roger Xu
Comprehensive compliance system overhaul addressing identified gaps
Dual compliance framework covering Chinese national security regulations and Western MNPI standards
Regional compliance teams with local regulatory knowledge in each major office
Expert screening adapted to both Chinese and international standards
Audit trail capabilities for client interactions
complianceExtended.regulatoryContext: In May 2023, Chinese state security authorities raided Capvision offices in Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, and Suzhou and featured the investigation in a 15-minute CCTV broadcast, accusing the firm of facilitating the transfer of sensitive information to foreign entities. The probe alleged that between 2017–2020, Capvision received over 2,000 remittances from over 100 overseas companies totaling more than $70 million. Capvision completed a government-supervised rectification in October 2023. This was part of a broader crackdown that also affected Bain & Company, Mintz Group, and the Big Four accounting firms in China. Note: This was a Chinese national security investigation, not a U.S. SEC action as sometimes incorrectly reported.

clientFit.narrative: Capvision is best suited for clients who need deep Asia-Pacific expertise, particularly those with investment or business interests in China and broader Asian markets. The firm's dual-market positioning makes it especially valuable for cross-border research where understanding both Asian and Western perspectives is important.

Research teams needing multilingual expert access across Asian languages
